findings.issue: McpDispatcher.render() calls handoff.resolve() OUTSIDE the runCatching that guards handoff.latest(). FileSlotAnnotationHandoff.resolve() throws IllegalArgumentException (asBareName) for any framePath/cropPath that is not a bare file name. The exception escapes handle(), escapes main()'s generateSequence{...}.forEach, and KILLS THE SERVER PROCESS with exit 1 and ZERO stdout — the client is left hanging on an unanswered request id. This directly contradicts three shipped claims: McpDispatcher's own KDoc ('a handoff that throws while answering a tool call is caught the same way rather than escaping (TAC-8)'), TAC-4 ('the loop keeps reading'), and plan NFR-4's 'resolve() path-traversal rejection' — the guard exists but converts a traversal attempt into a denial of service instead of a rejection. The existing test aThrowingHandoffYieldsAToolErrorAndTheDispatcherKeepsRunning cannot catch this because mcp-application's FakeAnnotationHandoff.resolve() never throws (TestFixtures.kt:83).
findings.evidence: REPRODUCED against the real installDist launcher. latest.json framePath set to '../../../../etc/passwd', then: printf '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_latest_annotation"}}\n{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}\n' | JAVA_OPTS=-Duser.home=<tmp> ./mcp-application/build/install/rectify-mcp/bin/rectify-mcp  ->  EXIT=1, stdout 0 lines, stderr: 'Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: handoff image name must be a bare file name, got: ../../../../etc/passwd / at FileSlotAnnotationHandoffKt.asBareName(FileSlotAnnotationHandoff.kt:104) / at FileSlotAnnotationHandoff.resolve(FileSlotAnnotationHandoff.kt:81) / at McpDispatcher.render$lambda$0$2(McpDispatcher.kt:145) / at McpDispatcher.render(McpDispatcher.kt:144)'. The id=2 tools/list that followed on stdin was never processed.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED by Stage 5 CR. render() moved inside a runCatching so a resolve() path-traversal rejection becomes a one-line isError:true tool error. Test fake fixed to throw like the real contract (the lenient double WAS the root cause) plus a regression test. Proven against the real installDist binary: exit 0, isError true, the process answers the following tools/list (was exit 1, zero stdout, loop dead).

findings.issue: The buildPrompt contradiction T-6 flagged IS shipping, and is worse than flagged. buildPrompt's trailer is unconditional: `"Attached: frame.png, $count crops, hierarchy.xml"`. Three independent lies are reachable: (a) a hierarchy-less send ships an envelope with hierarchyAvailable=false / hierarchyXml="" whose own prompt tells the agent hierarchy.xml is attached; (b) there is NEVER a file named hierarchy.xml in the send directory on ANY path — the hierarchy only ever rides inline in the envelope's hierarchyXml field, so the named attachment does not exist even on the happy path; (c) `$count crops` is the staged count, but EnvelopeAssembly emits cropPath=null (and no HandoffImage) for every annotation whose encode returned null, so the prompt can promise N crops when fewer or zero were attached. The same unconditional claim is duplicated in the completion toast: toastLabel() hardcodes '· frame + hierarchy ·' with no hierarchyAvailable parameter at all.

findings.issue: T-10's deliberate 'do not reset send to Idle on success' is NOT defensible as shipped, for a reason distinct from the one disclosed. SendStatusOverlay is visible whenever send != Idle, so the line that lingers over the resumed LIVE stage renders sendSteps(Sent, Streaming, Absent) = 'Streaming(Done) · Frozen(Frozen) · Dumping hierarchy(PENDING) · Sent(Done)' — a step-2 'Frozen' dot over a stage with nothing frozen, and a step-3 'Dumping hierarchy' back in Pending next to a completed step 4. It also breaks sendSteps' own documented invariant, which states verbatim: 'Every call to this function happens after MirrorUiState.frozen is already non-null'. That is now false on exactly the happy path. AC-19's 'Sent dot stays observable' is achievable without regressing steps 2 and 3.

findings.issue: AC-19's ordered sequence is not what the code can produce, independently of the missing demo. AC-19 asks for 'Streaming -> Frozen -> Dumping hierarchy -> Sent displays IN ORDER'. sendSteps drives step 3 off state.hierarchyStatus, and the hierarchy dump happens at FREEZE time, not during the send — so by the moment a send starts, step 3 is already Done (or already Absent/Pending and will never move). Only step 4 animates. The ordered four-step progression the AC describes is therefore unobservable: steps 1-3 are static from the first frame the overlay appears. This is documented honestly in sendSteps' KDoc ('the dump happens at freeze time, not during the send') — it is a declared behaviour divergence from the AC text, not a hidden bug, but AC-19 is verificationMethod=demo and the demo that would have surfaced it was not run.
findings.evidence: core/send/SendProjection.kt sendSteps(): step 3's state is `when (hierarchy) { Dumping -> Busy; Ready -> Done; Absent, Unavailable -> Pending }` with no dependence on `phase`; @param hierarchy KDoc: 'which drives step 3 independently of phase: the dump happens at freeze time, not during the send'. Only the step-4 `when (phase)` branch moves during a send.
findings.resolution: WAIVED AT A HUMAN GATE as partially satisfied. AC-19's four steps render with correct states and the failure variant works, but the animated in-order progression its wording implies is unachievable without moving the hierarchy dump out of freeze time and into the send - an architectural change the gate declined late in the spec. findings.issue: T-2's frozen-test-collision resolution verified, and the blast radius is slightly wider than the disclosure states. DeviceRepositoryImpl collapses to HierarchySnapshotModel.Empty (rawDump="") whenever `nodes.isEmpty() && densityDpi == 0` — BOTH conditions. So rawDump is dropped not only for a completely unparseable dump, but also for a structurally valid but node-less dump (e.g. `<hierarchy rotation="0"></hierarchy>`) on a device whose `wm density` also failed. Conversely a garbage dump on a device whose density DID parse keeps its rawDump and could forward an adb error message to the agent as a hierarchy. The consequence is acceptable in both directions (EnvelopeAssembly only reads rawDump when hierarchyStatus == Ready, and an Empty snapshot degrades to hierarchyAvailable=false for free), but the disclosed framing understates it.

aggregateDiffFindings.issue: Path-traversal guard is a crash, not a rejection, and it is on the unguarded side of the tool-call try/catch.
